content:
I just got a verification failure for my submission (based on the Github repo loefflerd / KN-scratch) saying:

AI review comments

  • The imported definitions of the elliptic-curve L-series, primitive character and conductor, and cusp-form q-expansion materially determine the statement. Their actual meanings cannot be checked against the Challenge documentation from the available pinned evidence. Provide access to the pinned Mathlib sources so these dependencies can be audited.

What should I do to "provide access to the pinned Mathlib sources"? (They are pinned at mathlib commit f6090c7, to match the current version of Tau Ceti.) Obviously Palomar does have access to the mathlib sources otherwise my project wouldn't build, but I'm mystified what I need to do in order to make this known to the AI review-bot.

(I have now been through a very large number of iterations of submitting this project to Tau Ceti – I think this is the 7th failed attempt – and each one takes ~ 2 hours to compile. I can't deny that this process is becoming a little frustrating. Is this kind of error rate normal?)

Yet another attempt just failed with the same error (after waiting > 2h for the slow single-threaded build to complete), despite explicitly giving a Github link to the pinned mathlib revision in the Challenge.lean docstring.

The AI review message seems to suggest copying across all the necessary mathlib files into my project repo; but that is clearly an utterly terrible idea, firstly because it would massively increase the build time, and secondly because those ~2.5 million lines of mirrored mathlib code would form part of the trust surface (my repo could include something that looked a lot like mathlib but had been subtly altered to change the meaning of the definitions).

I am mystified why this project is hitting this error, when virtually every other Palomar submission also relies on Mathlib to state its challenge file.

@Kim Morrison you are specified as the "initial point of contact" in the Palomar docs. Could you advise why Palomar's review process is serially rejecting my submission and what, if anything, can be done to fix it?
Also tagging @Matthew Ballard since I see you are currently logged in, & you are listed among Palomar's technical maintainers – if you could shed any light on this issue I would be very grateful.
Hi @David Loeffler, I work with Matt and I can try to help you with this. Thank you for the report, and sorry about the frustration!
I'm going through the failures right now, I'll let you know any findings soon. For now, I wouldn't bother resubmitting, it's likely we need some fixes on the Palomar side.

Okay, I have two related PRs that should fix this:

  • https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarReviewer/pull/162
  • https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarPolicy/pull/101

I'm reviewing the changes now, but it seems correct to me. @Kim Morrison please take a look when you have a second.

After they land, I'll bump hashes in https://github.com/PalomarRegistry/PalomarSubmissionState/pull/115, and your submission should then work.

Hi Aayush – that looks great, thanks for looking into this! Let me know if I can help at all.

If/when those PR's are merged, will my existing submission "come alive" again, or should I make a fresh submission from the same github repo?

PS: just to check, submissions "1argotnj3s6k" and "u39ev36dccxc" mentioned in your two PalomarRegistry PR's are my two latest attempts, right?

I'm asking because I actually couldn't find any public ID for my in-flight submissions – only the private deep link, and a run number for the mechanical verifier. This is obviously completely unrelated to the substance of the issue I encountered, but made reporting the issue here more difficult, because I couldn't concisely point to the submission that was failing. If the interface assigns an alphanumeric ID to new submissions, maybe it might be useful to show that ID to the author in the submission status page?
Hi @David Loeffler - are you past this message now? I started facing the same issue from yesterday
@Idris Ali Shaik I haven't tried to resubmit since Wednesday, I'm waiting for Aayush's pull requests to be merged. Until then I expect the issue will still be present.

@Aayush Rajasekaran @Kim Morrison Any progress on this? I see the Palomar PR's are still open. It has been a few days now, and others are apparently encountering the same failure.

(Idris Ali Shaik now seems to have deleted their account; but before doing so, they posted + deleted a message here, saying they had gotten around the review issue by copying a selection of mathlib definitions into an .md file in their project and referring to that in docstrings / readme. I am surprised that this works, to be honest, since the review agent has no way of checking that the contents of the .md file actually match mathlib.)

David Loeffler said:

Hi Aayush – that looks great, thanks for looking into this! Let me know if I can help at all.

If/when those PR's are merged, will my existing submission "come alive" again, or should I make a fresh submission from the same github repo?

Will do, thanks! Someone from the Palomar team should be able to trigger a re-review of your submission. You shouldn't need to make a fresh submission.

David Loeffler said:

PS: just to check, submissions "1argotnj3s6k" and "u39ev36dccxc" mentioned in your two PalomarRegistry PR's are my two latest attempts, right?

Yes, those are the ones.

David Loeffler said:

I'm asking because I actually couldn't find any public ID for my in-flight submissions – only the private deep link, and a run number for the mechanical verifier.

Good point -- I think the ID shows up when you make a submission, but it's missing from the status page. I'll open a PR for that too.

David Loeffler said:

Aayush Rajasekaran Kim Morrison Any progress on this? I see the Palomar PR's are still open. It has been a few days now, and others are apparently encountering the same failure.

I'll follow up with Kim in the maintainers channel -- I'm not comfortable merging this without her review. Thanks for your patience!

Good point -- I think the ID shows up when you make a submission, but it's missing from the status page. I'll open a PR for that too.

(Once I knew what I was looking for, I realised that it shows up as the title of the GitHub Action page for the build script for an in-flight submission.)

Hi, @David Loeffler

(I had posted this on other chat and moved here now.)
The workaround was posted by me, but moderators thought that is AI generated and banned me for 2 days :(

Here is the diff if someone wants to try: https://github.com/shaikidris/kkp-asymptotic-spectral-bound/commit/8aa258c7a0b06ae96cfa56018bddd60ee643efd5

Basically we added MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md with excerpts from the pinned Mathlib revision, including source and attribution
Also linked it to README.md and a comment pointing to Challenge.lean (This part was more like a guess)

We did not change any proof or dependency pins.
Hi @Aayush Rajasekaran - can you please check if this is somehow forcing the build script to find the Mathlib pins?

The pinned-library review fix is merged and deployed (thanks, Aayush!). David’s existing submission was recovered and is now registered: https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000022&version=1.
